Answers ADR 0149 rows 15, 34, 39 and 46 and the founder's 2026-09-19 answers for the notify page.

Five notification POST senders had no caller, and anyone could use them to send to any user id or address. They are no longer routes. send-email now goes through HouseEmailService. founder_questions.question: You said relay 400/403/422 are 'final'. As built, a final refusal releases the draft back to PENDING_APPROVAL and raises an error. The message bus then retries the send twice more. Each retry is refused by the gateway before anything is sent, and each is audited. After that the message goes to the dead-letter queue, and the gateway's reason is only in the logs and that queue, not on the draft. Is that what you meant by final, or should a final refusal close the draft for good with no retry? Today this touches nothing in production, because the orchestrator does not run there.

options.label: Keep as built
options.description: Final means 'definitely not sent': the draft is released for retry (the release side of the release-or-park question the records describe). Commit now. Cost: two useless refused retries per approval, and the reason is not shown on the draft.

options.label: Close, no retry
options.description: A new terminal status holds the gateway's sentence. No error is raised, so there is no retry. Cost: a new status value (check the table's constraint and a migration), a UI state to show it, and one more lane session.

options.label: Release quietly
options.description: Release the draft back to PENDING_APPROVAL but do not raise, so the bus does not retry, and log the sentence. Cost: a small code change. The refusal is still invisible on the draft, and a manager may re-approve the same failing send.

founder_questions.recommendation: Keep as built. It answers the question the records actually posed (release or park) with your 400/403/422 vs 401 split. The retries are harmless because the gateway refuses before anything is sent. The orchestrator is not live, so 'Close, no retry' can be a follow-up if you want a terminal state.
